name: Aktse-Pårte
estimatedTime: 7-9 hours per STF overview; 8-10 hours per STF detailed stage and Naturkartan
difficulty: Long, demanding/ansträngande and varied; field and route-app reports consistently treat this as a hard day, especially with Laitaure boat logistics, wet forest and the initial climb.
routeType: point-to-point mountain section with required Laitaure rowboat or motorboat crossing near the start

officialSources.name: STF Kungsleden Saltoluokta-Kvikkjokk route page
officialSources.evidence: Identifies stage 3 as STF Aktse Mountain Cabin to STF Pårte Mountain Cabin, 22 km and 7-9 hours. Describes rowing or motorboat over Laitaure before the long walk to Pårte and says the route enters Sarek National Park.

officialSources.name: STF Aktse-Pårte stage page
officialSources.evidence: Detailed STF stage page found by official-source lane, with 22 km, 8-10 hours, route description, Rittak shelter, difficult final descent in rain and Pårte no-shop caveat.
officialSources.caveat: URL slug uses ASCII 'parte' while page title and hut use Pårte.

officialSources.name: Naturkartan BD65 Aktse-Pårte
officialSources.evidence: Official route page/title Aktse-Pårte, Kungsleden / The King's Trail, with 23.0 km, 8-10 hours, 1 km boardwalk from Aktsestugan to Lajtavrre boat jetty, Laitaure rest cabin, Suobbatjåhkkå crossing, Jågge shelter and descent to Pårte.

officialSources.name: Naturkartan BD65 API / site 12895
officialSources.evidence: Public API, using page-discovered key, returned GeoJSON-like MultiLineString geometry with one line, 491 coordinates and published length 23.0 km.
officialSources.caveat: API geometry is land-route only, stored Pårte-to-Laitaure south, and excludes both Laitaure crossing and Aktse hut-to-jetty boardwalk.

officialSources.name: Naturkartan BD65 GPX
officialSources.evidence: Working GPX found by geometry lane; one segment, 625 trackpoints, no elevation and computed 19.657 km.
officialSources.caveat: Direct .kml and .geojson URLs returned 404; re-test GPX/API before later import.

commuteAccess.summary: Both official endpoints are roadless mountain huts. Aktse is reached by previous Kungsleden stages, by Sitoälvsbron private-road/taxi context plus trail, or through the Laitaure boat system. Pårte's closest direct public transport is Kvikkjokk about 16 km trail south, with bus connection toward Murjek/Jokkmokk in season.

startClosestCommutePoint.distanceFromEndpoint: about 1.0-1.1 km from STF Aktse by boardwalk/trail
startClosestCommutePoint.operatorOrNetwork: Länsstyrelsen Norrbotten rowboats; STF/private boatmaster Anne-Sophie Länta for motorboat service
startClosestCommutePoint.caveats: Not public road/transit. Rowboats are ice/season dependent and motorboat can be cancelled by severe weather; schedule/payment must be rechecked before travel.

endClosestCommutePoint.caveats: Exact 2026 operating days and stop coordinates need transit-planner verification before runtime import.

boatAccess.name: Aktse-Laitaure motorboat
boatAccess.operatorOrNetwork: Boatmaster Anne-Sophie Länta on STF behalf; local Aktse boat service
boatAccess.caveats: Schedule observed as June 19-September 14 with 09:00/17:00 Aktse-to-Laitaure and 09:15/17:15 Laitaure-to-Aktse, cash payment and severe-weather cancellation. Source currentness conflicts between 2025-05-07 and 2025-07-05 observations; verify 2026 directly.

hutCamping.notes: Service-fee camping possible if using hut facilities; tents farther away should respect STF guidance to avoid buildings and traffic areas.
Service-fee camping possible if using hut facilities; no shop at Pårte.

wildCamping.summary: Wild tenting is possible under allemansrätten/Sarek guidance, and Naturkartan mentions good tent places on open mountain, but no discrete on-route wild campsite coordinate was verified strongly enough for import.
caveats: Avoid hut compounds, private cabins, trail corridors, sensitive moss/lichen and reindeer disturbance areas.
Wet/boggy ground in forest and near boardwalks can make camping less practical.
Route crosses Sarek/Laponia for most of the section; follow protected-area guidance.

fire.summary: No confirmed public fireplace POI was found on this section. Laponia/Sarek guidance allows fires only within strict protected-area limits and fire bans override general allowances.
rules: Use only loose fallen sticks and branches where fires are allowed.
Do not break, cut or saw living/dead trees or shrubs and do not take birch bark.
Follow current fire bans and local protected-area rules.
Do not import off-section or unverified OSM firepit/campsite points near Sjábttjakjávrre as section-11 facilities.

protectedAreas.name: Sarek National Park
protectedAreas.evidence: STF says the route enters Sarek after the early forest/climb and continues there almost all the way to Pårte; Naturkartan says practically/almost the whole stage is in Sarek.
protectedAreas.caveat: Final selected-line GIS overlay is still needed. Do not assume Aktse hut, Laitaure boat crossing or immediate approach are inside Sarek without boundary confirmation.

protectedAreas.name: Laponia World Heritage
protectedAreas.evidence: Sarek is part of Laponia since 1996 and managed by Laponiatjuottjudus. The route traverses the southern Sarek marked-trail corridor.
protectedAreas.caveat: Natura 2000 site code/boundary details remain open for a later legal-boundary inventory.

dogs.summary: Dogs are generally prohibited in Sarek, but leashed dogs are allowed year-round on Kungsleden and generally January 1-April 30. Off-route summer/autumn side trips are not covered by the Kungsleden exception.

huntingFishing.summary: Hunting and fishing are prohibited in Sarek for ordinary visitors. Do not treat STF wording about fishing near Pårte as permission inside Sarek; outside park boundaries, Norrbotten permits and water-specific rules apply.

reindeer.summary: Do not intentionally disturb grazing reindeer or reindeer gathering/driving; wait or walk around animals rather than pushing through.

dronesAircraft.summary: Drone/aircraft wording has tension between Laponia public guidance and current consolidated rules. Conservative import guidance: do not present drone use as allowed in/over Sarek without checking Länsstyrelsen/Laponiatjuottjudus current permission requirements.

organizedActivities.summary: Organized activities, competitions, camps, recurring organized tours, larger events, scientific investigations and dog-sled travel require permission.

seasonalityAndCurrentness: STF Aktse and STF Pårte 2026 opening periods: 2026-02-27 to 2026-04-19 and 2026-06-18 to 2026-09-13.
Aktse-Laitaure motorboat page remains until-further-notice 2025 information; recheck 2026 schedule, payment and weather cancellation policy.
Laitaure rowboats are normally placed around midsummer/no later than July 1 and remain until late September, depending on ice and field setup.

Laponia current notice dated 2026-02-12 said western Laponia had relatively little snow and Sarek/Badjelannda bridges had been lifted for winter 2025/2026; no summer 2026 replacement confirmation was found by the rules lane.
No official Aktse-Pårte-specific closure or reroute was found as of 2026-04-29, but current pages are dynamic.
routeHazards: Laitaure is a large, exposed lake; motorboat can be cancelled in severe weather and rowing can be slow/hard in wind/current.
First major ascent after Laitaure is steep and can feel strenuous early in the day.
Wet forest, marsh/bog, old/rotten planks and muddy descents recur in field reports.
Bridges are generally mapped, but field reports mention awkward steep perforated-metal bridge stairs for dogs/loads and higher rivers after rain.
Poor/variable mobile coverage at Pårte; emergency phones should be treated as safety services, not ordinary phone coverage.

conditionReports.summary: Recent field reports describe the day as Laitaure boat, forest, marsh/bog, streams, steep climb, open plateau and descent to Pårte, with most ascent in the first 8 km.

conditionReports.source: 2024-12-21 field report summarized by field-report lane
conditionReports.summary: Describes local first boat, lush forests, marshlands, glacial streams, steep climbs and high plateaus.
Metrics conflict: AllTrails 2025 lists about 19.6 km / 657 m / hard, while Outdooractive lists about 22.6 km / 479 m. Official 22 km / 7-9 h remains the baseline.

conditionReports.source: We12Travel and Distant North reports summarized by field-report lane
conditionReports.summary: Repeated wet forest/swamp, rocky trail, rotten plank and muddy/wet-shoe warnings.

conditionReports.source: 2025 Reddit reports summarized by field-report lane
conditionReports.summary: Reports of hard rain/cold near Laitaure, sideways current and about 45 minutes for rowboat crossing, possible triple-crossing delay and crowding at the 09:00 boat.
conditionReports.caveat: Reddit reports are useful field-currentness clues but should not override official boat/current-status sources.

conditionReports.source: 2025 Reddit/Calazo shelter caveat summarized by field-report lane
conditionReports.summary: One Calazo-marked shelter between Aktse and Pårte reportedly was not found. Do not rely on unverified mapped shelters beyond Laitaure and Jågge/Rittak.
Calicivirus affected huts including Aktse and Pårte in August 2023 with temporary service changes; no current 2026 closure/reroute found.
conditionReports.caveat: Historical only; recheck STF current notices before publication.

sourceContradictions.details: STF overview says 22 km / 7-9 h; STF detailed stage says 22 km / 8-10 h; Naturkartan says 23.0 km / 8-10 h; STF Aktse facility text says Pårte is about 24 km south; route apps vary around 19.6-22.6 km.
sourceContradictions.impact: Use STF overview 22 km / 7-9 h as display baseline for section order, while preserving 8-10 h and 23/24 km contradictions for normalization.
